articleTitle: SMQTT: A Lightweight Clock Synchronization Algorithm for IoT Devices Using MQTT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Advancements in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and cyber-physical systems have driven the development of Industry 4.0, which has led to the emergence of advanced cloud-based applications. The web applications connect the field IIoT devices to ‘the Internet’. The adequate performance of web applications depends on how seamlessly devices communicate and synchronize. The IIoT devices prominently use Message Queueing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) for machine to machine (M2M) communication. MQTT implements publish-subscribe-based broker architecture that distributes a common timebase to client devices. Such one-way time transfer methods are less accurate and often introduce synchronization errors. While existing time synchronization methods for field IIoT end devices, e.g., Simple Network Time Protocol (SNTP), provide adequate synchronization based on two-way delay transfer methods, their performance degrades significantly with deteriorating network conditions. To address these synchronization challenges, we propose SMQTT, a scalable, software-based, lightweight clock synchronization method for IIoT end devices utilizing MQTT-based M2M communication. The proposed method effectively leverages the broker architecture to implement a two-way delay-based synchronization algorithm. We conducted measurements in network deployments to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. The results demonstrate that SMQTT surpasses both SNTP and state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy. Specifically, in our measurements under poor network conditions, SMQTT achieves synchronization performance improvements of 94% and 73% compared to SNTP and the state-of-the-art method, respectively.

articleTitle: A Solution for Wireless Precision Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: In this manuscript we present a wireless time synchronization method based on wireless two-way interferometry (Wi-Wi). The need for precision time synchronization is growing as more systems are seeking more efficiency gains. Traditionally, synchronization has been done via wire (copper or fiber) due to the simplicity and determinism. This becomes an issue for applications where using a wire is not feasible due to the mobility or accessibility to the infrastructure. Wireless methods such as Wi-Fi(802.11), Bluetooth or Zigbee are unable to get precision time synchronization because the system architecture and the lack of using phase information. Our method utilizes the phase information between the transmitted signal and received signal. This provides the necessary synchronization. With the use of a unique packet analysis, synchronization is provided. We plan to implement this technology of the receiver carrier board(RCB) to be used on the Time Card.

articleTitle: National Time Scale of Bosnia and Herzegovina as Timing and Synchronization Source in Critical Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: In the following paper we elaborate the example of building national key infrastructure for time distribution and synchronization of critical end-users, presenting briefly the international timescale and its local realization as the most accurate time source in the country, the transport technology background and use cases in order to demonstrate advantages compared to the currently most used satellite systems solutions. We describe the experimental realization of a system developed for the distribution of time and frequency reference signals, synchronized with the national time scale, to the end user in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The architecture of the national timescale system and dissemination link technology is described. The achieved performances are evaluated in terms of accuracy, stability and availability, with the aim to demonstrate robust alternative time and synchronization service as a important segment of critical infrastructure for industry, business and the digitized society. A model for building the core infrastructure for distribution network is proposed.

articleTitle: Linuxptp Servo Optimization for Network Adapters with High-Precision Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Network Adapters with high-precision oscillators (typically Oven Controlled Oscillator, OCXO) and Global Navigational Satellite System (GNSS) receivers appeared on the market for time and frequency synchronization-related use cases in telecommunications and data center applications. They are designed for the grandmaster clock role primarily; however, we introduced alternative use cases for these cards in this paper, which also use time Receiver role (IEEE 1588g-2022). The user-space software framework for these cards is provided by the Linux PTP (linuxptp) project typically, in which ptp4l is the IEEE 1588 compliant clock implementation. A servo (controller) sets the PTP Hardware Clock (PHC) according to the network-acquired offset samples in the timeReceiver role of ptp4l, which can be selected from a set of implemented servos (pi, linreg, ntpshm, nullf). This paper investigates how the relevant servos (pi, linreg) behave in normal timeReceiver/synchronized operation and how the servo selection and configuration influence the holdover mode. The results are relevant to the proposed use cases. The investigation was done by comparing the performance of the Intel E810-XXVDA4 Network Adapter and an E810-XXVDA4T with a high-precision OCXO and Digital Phase-Locked Loop (DPLL). The presence of two different oscillators gives a very special insight into how the oscillator and servo influence synchronization and holdover performance.

articleTitle: Best Practices in Industrial Time Dissemination
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Technological advances in the last few decades have radically changed and increased the world's requirements for accurate, traceable timing. This paper describes how our company has approached the challenge of global industrial time dissemination in the new technological landscape, and present what we believe are best practices, in the interest of provoking discussion and industry-wide consensus.

articleTitle: Comparison of Time Synchronization Sources for PMU Calibration Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Monitoring and control applications for modern power systems shall rely on a distributed and synchronized measurement infrastructure. In this context, the calibration of new generation Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) is becoming a challenge for National Metrological Institutes, and requires the minimization of any uncertainty contribution. In this paper, we discuss how different reference clocks may affect the synchronization of the PMU calibrator to the Coordinated Universal Time. The adoption of a White Rabbit time distribution allows for reducing by at least a factor five the synchronization uncertainty.

articleTitle: Characterization of Time Error and Time Holdover Utilizing Estimation Calculations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: An important approach to building a robust system for delivering accurate time couples a source of UTC such as GNSS with an autonomous frequency source such as an atomic oscillator. Analytic methods have been developed that optimize system time delivery when UTC time is not available. These same methods can be applied in two additional important ways. First, they can be used to select the best frequency sources in a population for system deployment. Second, they can be used for monitoring an active system to indicate how long that system can hold time within required bounds when operating autonomously. This paper will summarize these statistical analytic tools and show their use in selection and monitoring.

articleTitle: Using Higher Stability Oscillators for NICs and CPUs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: This work shows the value of using a high stability oscillator such as a TCXO (temperature compensated oscillator) or OCXO (oven controlled oscillator) in network interface cards (NICs) and/or central processing units (CPUs). This value can be expanded to switches and other types of network hardware. Different test scenarios using Precision Time Measurement (PTM) -simply PTP on the PCIe bus involving the device and the root complex-were used on customized hardware (a pair of NUC11TNH devices).

articleTitle: Simple Precision Time Protocol (SPTP)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: In this manuscript we describe a simplified implementation of the Precision Time Protocol (PTP) which is called Simple PTP (SPTP). Existing unicast profiles come with various extensions such as subscription, signaling messages, flow control and authentication methods. These extensions come at the price of increased complexity and performance penalties. However, in a typical data center application most of the extensions are unnecessary and often impossible to use. We tested the SPTP implementation at scale and showed that it is functional in comparison to mainstream unicast PTP implementations using G8265.1 and G8275.2 profiles.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Advanced Synchronization Capabilities of PTM Enabled Hardware
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: The implementation of Precision Time Measurement (PTM) within time aware networking devices will work to achieve the precise time synchronization required for next generation applications. The PTM protocol is currently the only method to transfer the precise timing information from the network interface card to the CPU. This will allow software applications to run under the same strict timing boundaries currently limited to the network layer. Through this study we will demonstrate this accuracy and measure, for the first time, the effect of PTM on a commercial hardware equipment setup.

articleTitle: Holdover Improvements to the linuxptp Servo for Network Adapters with High-Precision Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: The Linux PTP Project (linuxptp) provides the de facto standard application framework for Precision Time Protocol (IEEE 1588 and its profiles) implementation on Linux. The ptp4l user-space application of linuxptp realizes PTP-compliant clocks (Ordinary, Boundary, or Transparent). The ptp4l application disciplines a timeReceiver clock with a servo algorithm to a time Transmitter clock. It is possible in regular operation that ptp4l goes from timeReceiver role to time Transmitter role, in which case the system is in holdover mode, i.e., it keeps time based only on its oscillator, and that kept time is transmitted to time Receivers over the PTP protocol. The holdover performance of ptp4l is not investigated in detail up to now; however, new network adapters and add-on cards with High-Performance Oscillators (HPO) are developed for applications in which it is a common mode of operation. The paper presents and investigates modified servo algorithms for ptp4l to improve holdover performance and compares them to the built-in servos. The new algorithms are tested with an Intel E810-XXVDA4T Network Adapter with HPO. The results apply to other network adapters with HPO in our view, and they can also improve the performance of regular Network Adapters in all application fields. The new servo implementations are planned to be submitted for inclusion into the linuxptp code base.

articleTitle: Exploring Wireless Clock Synchronization with OCP-TAP Time Cards and RTL-SDRs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Wireless clock synchronization between data centers is a topic of interest due to a variety of applications and services in the cloud needing to fuse data based on a common time reference. The need to discipline local clocks at each data center presents a synchronization challenge for an application or service when Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is disrupted. We seek to explore a resilient wireless clock synchronization approach leveraging RTL-SDRs and Internet of Things (IoT) when GNSS is disrupted on the Time Cards part of the Open Compute Project. The Open Compute Project - Time Appliances Project (OCP-TAP) Time Cards provide an open timing architecture and a source of time for data centers leveraging a GNSS receiver built into a Receiver Carrier Board (RCB) and include a stable time reference (i.e. CSAC or TCXO) when GNSS signals are disrupted. We seek to explore how best to wirelessly synchronize a network of OCP-TAP Time Cards with RTL-SDRs to wirelessly distribute a common clock source between OCP-TAP Time Cards when GNSS signals are unavailable. Our wireless clock synchronization approach seeks to support the development of a modified RCB that combines a GNSS chipset with an RTL-SDR and an IoT device to provide wireless two-way interferometry (Wi-Wi). Fusing an IoT chipset with an RTL-SDR and a GNSS receiver provides an inexpensive way to add wireless clock synchronization between OCP-TAP Time Cards if GNSS signals are disrupted. An RTL-SDR based RCB primarily functions to provide clock synchronization information between the OCP-TAP Time Cards for relative clock synchronization across a network of OCP-TAP Time Cards based on the exchange of messages between the IoT devices. A LoRa based IoT device is considered to provide the wireless clock synchronization signal between OCP-TAP Time Cards but any type of IoT device that can be captured in the frequency range of the RTL-SDR is sufficient for this approach.

articleTitle: Synchronisation Methods for the Converging Telecom and Data Centre Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Data centre synchronisation is a critical aspect of modern data centre operations and management, ensuring that various elements in the data centres are operating at a certain level of time consistency. With the increasing reliance on distributed data centres for 5G-related cellular communications, cloud computing, big data analytics, and other large-scale applications, achieving data centre synchronisation has become more complex and challenging. With 5G, the data centre must synchronise to radios for effective and collaborative operations. Time-sensitive applications depend on the networks deployed in the Data centres to guarantee the timing. This paper presents the various techniques used in achieving synchronisation within data centres.

articleTitle: Exploiting Accurate Ultra Wide Band Time Synchronization at the Application Level in Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: With the increasing demand for precision and accuracy in embedded systems, reliable time synchronization has become an absolute necessity. Traditional time synchronization methods, such as wired connections or wireless protocols that operate in specific frequency bands, frequently have interference, range, and synchronization accuracy limitations. Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) communication technology has emerged as a promising solution for highly accurate time synchronization in embedded systems in recent years. Several solutions have been proposed in the scientific literature that enable fully accurate time synchronizations to be obtained using UWB as the transmission medium. However, using this time information in embedded systems remains difficult without specialized and expensive hardware solutions. This paper proposes a solution for utilizing the accurate time obtained using commercial UWB transceiver and peripherals which are commonly found in all microcontroller architectures. The feasibility of the proposed solution was evaluated using an ESP32 microcontroller running the ZephyrOS Real Time Operating System (RTOS) as a platform. The results show that this solution can achieve time synchronization with accuracy less than a microsecond at the application level, demonstrating the validity of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Precision Time Protocol Profile for Datacenter Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: This paper describes the OCP-TAP Datacenter PTP Profile, developed for large-scale, high-performance datacenter-based applications. The paper first covers datacenter network topology and then illustrates the specific requirements for this industry vertical via the distributed database system use case. Building upon those requirements, the paper then covers the Datacenter PTP Profile and the main attributes to enable a reliable time distribution and synchronization service across the infrastructure of a datacenter network. Finally, related workstreams are discussed ahead of the conclusion.

articleTitle: Equivalence of JST Algorithm and Kalman Filtering Algorithm for Time Scale Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Existing studies have established two different algorithms, the Kalman filtering algorithm and the Japan Standard Time (JST) algorithm, for generating reliable time scales. However, the relations between those two methods have not been clarified. In this paper, we mathematically clarify the equivalence of the averaged atomic time of JST-algo and Kalman filtering algorithm. In particular, we reveal the fact that the averaged atomic time of JST-algo does not depend on the measurement noise even though there is no filtering procedure in the algorithm. Furthermore, the prediction error of Kalman filtering algorithm is rigorously shown by using the prediction error regarding an observable state space. It is mathematically shown that when the covariance matrices of system noises are identical for all atomic clocks, then considering equal averaging weights for the clocks is a necessary and sufficient condition to ensure the equivalence between JST-algo and Kalman filtering algorithm. A numerical example comparing the runtime of JST-algo and Kalman filtering algorithm is provided to illustrate the efficacy of JST-algo.

articleTitle: Automated Root Cause Analysis in Time-Sensitive Networks Based on Fault Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Time-Sensitive networking plays a major role in the convergence of IT and OT in the use cases of Industry 4.0. The available mechanisms of TSN, such as Frame Preemption (IEEE 802.1Q), Time Synchronization (IEEE 802.1AS), and Enhancements for Scheduled Traffic (IEEE 802.1Q), make devices and networks more complex when they first start up, run, or fail. Fault detection and diagnosis require experience and expert knowledge to find the root cause of faults and troubleshoot them. However, unlike other communication technologies, there is no information about possible faults or errors, how to recognize errors, or how to handle errors in time-sensitive mechanisms. Therefore, a fully automated approach to identifying the underlying cause of a malfunction is required to aid network administrators in the event of a malfunction, thereby minimizing downtime. How can an automated root cause analysis system in time-sensitive networking be realized, and how can faulty configuration of scheduled traffic be automatically detected? This work describes a concept for automated root cause analysis in time-sensitive networks based on fault models (SARCAI-TSN), and investigates the possible symptoms of faulty Frame Preemption and Scheduled Traffic configuration with a test setup. Furthermore, it presents a scheduled traffic anomaly detection algorithm for the detection of faulty scheduled traffic configurations. This research provides assistance to both vendors and users in fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) in Time-Sensitive Networking.

articleTitle: Welcome
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS)
abstract: Welcome to the 2023 International IEEE Symposium on Precision Clock Synchronization for Measurement, Control, and Communication (ISPCS). This year, we have the privilege of being able to gather at the National Physical Laboratory, one of the world's oldest Metrology institutes and the site of one of the very first Atomic Clocks in the world.
